TO BE PUBLISHED IN THE NEXT
ISSUE OF BALOCHISTAN GAZETTE.
.
BALOCHISTAN PROVINCIAL ASSEMBLY SECRETARIAT
NOTIFICATION.
Dated Quetta, the 30th March, 2021.
No.PAB/Legis:V(06)/2020. The Balochistan University of Agriculture, Quetta
Bill, 2020 (Bill No. 06 of 2020), having been passed by the Provincial Assembly of
Balochistan on 22nd March, 2021 and assented to by the Governor Balochistan,
on 29th March, 2021 is hereby published as an Act of the Balochistan Provincial
Assembly.
The Balochistan University of Agriculture, Quetta Act No VIII of 2021.
AN
ACT
to provide for the establishment of the Balochistan
University of Agriculture Quetta.
Preamble. WHEREAS it is expedient to establish the Balochistan University of
Agriculture Quetta for promoting the advancement and dissemination of
knowledge in the fields of agriculture, livestock, social and natural sciences
and humanities and to form an organized scientific infrastructure for teaching
and research for the development of diversified agriculture and allied sciences
in the Balochistan Province.
It is hereby enacted as follows:-
CHAPTER I
PRELIMINARY
Short title and 1. (1) This Act may be called the Balochistan University of
Commencement. Agriculture, Quetta Act, 2021.
(2) It shall come into force at once.
Definitions. 2. In this Act, unless the subject or context otherwise requires, the
following expressions shall have the meanings hereby respectively
assigned to them, that is to say–
(a) “Act” means the Balochistan University of Agriculture Quetta
Act, 2021;
(b) “Academic Council” means the Academic Council of the
University;
1
(c) “Advanced Studies and Research Board” means the
Advanced Studies and Research Board constituted under this
Act;
(d) “Affiliated college” means a college or institute affiliated with
the University but not maintained or administered by it;
(e) “Alumni” means former students of the Balochistan
Agriculture College, Quetta and Balochistan University of
Agriculture, Quetta;
(f) “Authority” means an Authority of the University as
specified under section 21 of the Act ;
(g) “Chairperson” means the head of a department, Principal of
a constituent college or director of an institute;
(h) “Chancellor” means the Governor of Balochistan;
(i) “Commission” means the Higher Education Commission set
up under the Higher Education Commission Ordinance, 2002
(LIII of 2002);
(j) “Constituent college” means a college maintained and
administered by the University;
(k) “Controller of Examinations” means the Controller of
Examinations of the University;
(l) “Dean” means the head of a faculty of the University;
(m) “Department” means a teaching department maintained and
administered by the University in the prescribed manner;
(n) “Disciplinary Committee” means the Disciplinary
Committee constituted under this Act.
(o) “Faculty” means an administrative and academic unit of the
University consisting of one or more departments, institutes
or constituent colleges;
(p) “Finance and Planning Committee” means the Finance and
Planning Committee constituted under this Act;
(q) “Government” means the Government of Balochistan;
(r) “Institute” means an institute established, maintained and
administered by the University;
(s) “Prescribed” means prescribed by rules, statutes or regulations;
(t) “Pro-Vice Chancellor” means the Pro-Vice Chancellor of
the University;
(u) “Principal” means the head of a college;
(v) “Province” means the Balochistan Province;
(w) “Registrar” means the Registrar of the University;
(x) “Review Panel” means the Review Panel set up by the
Chancellor in accordance with the provisions of the Act;
(y) “Senate” means the Senate of University;
(z) “Statutes”, “regulations” and “rules” mean respectively the
statutes, regulations and rules made under the Act
(aa) “Syndicate” means the Syndicate of the University;
2
(bb) “University Teacher” includes a Professor, Associate
Professor, Assistant Professor and Lecturer, engaged
whole-time by the University or by constituent or affiliated
college and such other person as may be prescribed;
(cc) “Treasurer” means the Treasurer of the University;
(dd) “Librarian” means the Librarian of the University;
(ee) “University” means the University of Agriculture, Quetta;
(ff) “Vice Chancellor” means the Vice Chancellor of the
University;
(gg) “Director” means head of the Teaching and Administrative
Division or an institute established by the University;
(hh) “Research Officer” means a person engaged whole time by
the University for research and equivalent in rank to a
University teacher; and
(ii) “Selection Committee” means the Selection Committee
constituted under this Act;
(jj) “Erstwhile college” means the Balochistan Agriculture
College, Quetta, which on commencement of this Act shall
be erstwhile college.
CHAPTER II
THE UNIVERSITY
Incorporation. 3. (1) The Government shall, by notification, reconstitute the
Balochistan Agriculture College Quetta as the Balochistan University of
Agriculture Quetta.
(2) The University shall be a body corporate by the name of the
Balochistan University of Agriculture Quetta having perpetual succession
and a common seal with power to acquire, hold and dispose of property
and shall, by the aforesaid name, sue and be sued.
(3) The Government may, by notification, affiliate any of its
post graduate and degree colleges with the University.
(4) The University may, with the approval of Government,
open and administer a sub-campus of the University.
(5) The University shall consist of the following:-
(a) The Chancellor;
(b) The Vice Chancellor;
(c) The Pro-Vice Chancellor;
(d) The Members of an Authority established under
section 21 of this Act;
(e) Chairpersons and Deans;
(f) The Teachers and students of the University; and
3
(g) Officers and members of the staff of the University.
Transfer of Assets, 4 . (1) All properties, rights and interests of whatever kind, used,
Liabilities, enjoyed, possessed, owned or vested in, or held in by and all liabilities
Employees of subsisting against the Balochistan Agriculture College, Quetta shall stand
Balochistan transferred to the University.
Agriculture
College, Quetta.
2. All regular employees of Balochistan Agriculture College,
Quetta serving in any capacity, before commencement of this Act, shall
stand transferred for service to the university, however, they shall remain
as Civil Servants and their services shall be governed under Balochistan
Civil Servants Act 1974 (Act No. IX of 1974) and Rules framed there
under:
Provided that no further appointments / recruitments shall be made in
Balochistan Agriculture College, Quetta after the commencement of this
Act.
Provided further that their inter-se Seniority shall be maintained as
they have prior to their transfer.
Provided further also that any question arising with the transfer of
regular employees of Balochistan Agriculture College Quetta serving in
any capacity for transfer to the Balochistan University of Agriculture
Quetta may be referred to the Government.
(3) The University may give option to the employees of the
erstwhile college to join the university having required qualification or
experience as the case may be and as prescribed:
Provided that the option once availed shall be final and such
employee shall cease to be a Civil Servant and the benefits there under as
provided in sub section (2), however, the employee shall be entitled for
refund of his/her actual contribution under GP Fund, Benevolent Fund and
Group Insurance.
Provided further that employees of the erstwhile college shall be
given preference, who apply for the posts in the university and fulfilled the
prescribed qualification and experience of the university.
4
Powers, Purpose 5. (1) The University shall have the following powers, purpose and
and functions of functions:-
the University.
(a) to provide for education in agriculture, livestock, social
and natural sciences, humanities and such branches of
knowledge as it may deem fit, and to make provisions
for research, service to the society and for the
application, advancement and dissemination of
knowledge in such manner as it may determine;
(b) to establish, maintain and administer a department,
constituent college or an institute;
(c) to establish and support other facilities for education,
training and research;
(d) to prescribe courses of studies;
(e) to decide teaching methods and strategies in order to
ensure the most effective educational and training
programmes;
(f) to hold examinations in the prescribed manner and, if
a person qualifies the examination, award degree,
diploma, certificate and other academic distinction to
the person;
(g) to prescribe the terms and conditions of employment
of the officers, teachers and other employees of the
University;
(h) to engage, where necessary, a person on contract for
specified duration and to specify the terms of the
engagement;
(i) to provide career counselling and job search services
to the students and alumni;
(j) to maintain linkages with alumni;
(k) to provide and support the academic development of
the faculty of the University;
(l) to confer degree on a person who has successfully
conducted research in the prescribed manner;
(m) to institute Professorship, Associate Professorship,
Assistant Professorship and Lectureship or any other
post and may appoint a person on the post;
(n) to create a post for research, extension, administration
or other related purposes and appoint a person to the
post;
(o) to institute and award financial assistance to students
in need, fellowships, scholarships, bursaries, medals
and prizes in the prescribed manner;
(p) to provide for the residence of the students, establish
and maintain halls of residence and may approve or
licence premises for hostel, lodging or boarding
place;
5
(q) to maintain order, discipline and security in a campus of
the University;
(r) to promote the extracurricular and recreational
activities of the students and make arrangements for
promoting health and general welfare of the students;
(s) to demand and receive such fees and other charges as
it may determine;
(t) to perform any other prescribed or ancillary function;
(u) to institute programs for the exchange of students and
teachers between the University and any other
university, educational institution or research
organization inside as well as outside of Pakistan;
(v) to develop and implement fund-raising plans;
(w) to accept an examination and the period of study spent
by a student of the University at any other university
or place of learning equivalent to an examination or
period of study of the University and may withdraw
such acceptance;
(x) to cooperate with a public authority, university or
private organization in the prescribed manner;
(y) to make provision for research, advisory or
consultancy services and enter into arrangements with
any other institution, public or private body,
commercial or industrial enterprise in the prescribed
manner;
(z) to receive and manage property transferred and
grants, contributions made to the University and to
invest any fund in the manner as it may deem fit;
(aa) to print and publish research or work;
(bb) to admit any college or other educational institution to
its privileges or withdraw such privileges in the
prescribed manner;
(cc) to affiliate or disaffiliate a college or any other
educational institution in the prescribed manner; and
(dd) to exercise any power ancillary to the above powers
or as may be prescribed; and
(ee) to recognize selected members of the teaching staff of
affiliated colleges or educational institutions admitted
to the privileges of the University or such other
persons as it may deem fit as University teachers;
University to be 6. (1) The University shall be open to all students either gender and
open for all of whatever religion, race, creed, class or color or domicile and no person
students’ shall be denied the privileges of the University on the grounds of a person
admissions. on religion, race, creed, class or color or domicile.
6
Provided that the existing policy of admission of Under Graduate
students of erstwhile college shall continue in Faculty of Agriculture of
the university until modified by the Senate.
Provided further that the scholarship of the Under Graduate
students admitted in the erstwhile college shall be continue at the existing
rates before the commencement of this Act, until their graduation.
(2) An increase in any fee or charge that is in excess of ten percent
per annum on an annual basis from the last such increase may not be made
except in special circumstances, and only with the approval of the Senate.
(3) The University shall institute financial aid programs for
students in need, to the extent considered feasible by the Senate given the
resources available, so as to enable admission and access to the University
and the various opportunities provided by it to be based on merit rather
than ability to pay:
Provided that the University may institute self-finance schemes,
not covering more than ten percent of the total number of candidates on
merit in any campus taught course or research-based program of study.
(4) The University shall exercise the powers conferred on it by
or under this Act within the territorial limits of the Balochistan Province
and in respect of the institution over which it has jurisdiction in accordance
with law.
Jurisdiction. 7. The jurisdiction of the University shall be restricted to the
Balochistan Province.
Teaching of the 8. (1) All recognized teaching in various courses shall be conducted
University. by the University or the colleges in the prescribed manner and may include
lectures, tutorials, discussions, seminars, demonstrations, distance
learning and other methods of instruction as well as practical work in the
laboratories, workshops and other governmental or private organizations.
(2) The authority responsible for organizing recognized
teaching shall be such as may be prescribed.
(3) Notwithstanding anything contained in any other law for the
time being in force the research fields /farms and other facilities of the
Agriculture Research and Extension wings of Agriculture and Cooperative
Department shall be available for the students and faculty of the
University.
7
(4) The Government of Balochistan, Finance Department shall continue to
provide operating expenses as grant to the university equivalent to the
amount provided to the erstwhile college before the commencement of
this Act with annual increase as deemed appropriate.
Provided that the employees related expenses of erstwhile college
shall be budgeted separately under the university.
CHAPTER -III
OFFICERS OF THE UNIVERSITY
Officers of the 9. The following shall be the officers of the University, namely:-
University.
(a) the Chancellor;
(b) the Vice Chancellor;
(c) the Pro-Vice Chancellor;
(d) the Deans;
(e) the Principals of the constituent colleges;
(f) the Chairpersons of the teaching departments;
(g) the Registrar;
(h) the Treasurer;
(i) the Controller of Examinations;
(j) the Director QEC;
(k) the Director Advanced Studies & Research Board;
(l) the Librarian;
(m) the Deputy Controller of Examination;
(n) the Deputy Registrar;
(o) the Director Planning and Development;
(p) the Assistant Controller of Examination;
(q) the Assistant Registrar;
(r) the Resident Auditor;
(s) the Director Students Affairs;
(t) the Director Legal Affairs; and
(u) such other persons as may be prescribed by the Statues or
Regulations to be the principal officers of the University.
Chancellor. 10. (1) The Governor of Balochistan shall be the Chancellor of the
University and Chairperson of the Senate.
(2) The Chancellor when present shall preside over the
convocation of the University and meeting of the Senate. In his absence
the Vice Chancellor shall preside over the convocation.
8
(3) The University may, subject to the prior approval of the
Chancellor, confer honorary degree.
(4) The Chancellor shall appoint the members of the Senate, the
Vice Chancellor and Pro Vice Chancellor from amongst the persons
recommended by the Selection Committee set up for this purpose.
(5) If the Chancellor is satisfied that serious irregularity or
mismanagement with respect to the affairs of the University has occurred,
he may:-
(a) as regards proceedings of the Senate, direct that
specified proceedings be reconsidered and
appropriate action taken within one month of the
direction having been issued:
Provided that if the Chancellor is satisfied that no
reconsideration has been carried out or that the
reconsideration has failed to address the concern
expressed he may, after calling upon the Senate to
show cause in writing, appoint a five member Review
Panel to examine and report to the Chancellor on the
functioning of the Senate. The report of the Review
Panel shall be submitted within such time as may be
prescribed by the Chancellor. The Review Panel shall
be drawn from persons of eminence in academics and
in the fields of law, accountancy and administration;
and
(b) as regards proceedings of any Authority or with
respect to matters within the competence of any
Authority other than the Senate, direct the Syndicate
to exercise powers under section 25.
(6) Subject to this Act, the Chancellor may approve the draft
statutes submitted by the Senate or refer the statutes back to the Senate for
reconsideration.
(7) In the performance of all the functions under this Act, the
Chancellor shall act and shall be bound in the same manner as the
Governor of Balochistan acts and is bound under clause (1) of Article 105
of the Constitution of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan.
Removal from the 11. (1) The Chancellor may, upon the recommendation of the Review
senate. Panel, remove any person from the membership of the Senate on the
ground that such person:
9
a) has become of unsound mind; or
b) has become incapacitated to function as
member of the Senate; or
c) has been convicted by a court of law for an
offence involving moral turpitude; or
d) has absented himself/herself from two consecutive
meetings without just cause; or
e) has been guilty of misconduct, including use of position
for personal advantage of any kind, or gross
inefficiency in the performance of functions.
(2) The Chancellor shall remove any person from the
membership of the Senate on a resolution calling for the removal of such
person supported by at least three-fourths of the membership of the
Senate:
Provided that before passing such resolution, the Senate shall
provide the member concerned a fair hearing:
Provided further that the provisions of this action shall not be
applicable to the Vice Chancellor in his capacity as a member of the
Senate.
Vice Chancellor. 12. (1) There shall be a Vice-Chancellor of the University who shall
be qualified in any relevant field of the University and shall be appointed
on such terms and conditions as may be prescribed.
(2) The Vice-Chancellor shall be the chief executive officer of
the University responsible for all administrative and academic functions
of the University and for ensuring that the provisions of the Act, Statutes,
Regulations and Rules are faithfully observed in order to promote the
general efficiency and good order of the University. The Vice-Chancellor
shall have all powers prescribed for this purpose, including administrative
control over the officers, teachers and other employees of the University.
(3) The Vice-Chancellor shall, if present, be entitled to attend
any meeting of any Authority or body of the University.
(4) The Vice-Chancellor may, in an emergency that in his
opinion requires immediate action ordinarily not in the competence of the
Vice-Chancellor, take such action and forward, within seventy-two hours,
a report of the action taken to the members of the Emergency Committee
of the Senate, to be set up by Statute, The Emergency Committee may
either confirm the action taken or direct such further action as is
considered appropriate.
10
(5) The Vice-Chancellor shall also have the following powers,
namely:-
(a) to direct teachers, officers and other employees of
the University to take up such assignments in
connection with examination, administration and
such other activities in the University as he may
consider necessary for the purposes of the
University;
(b) to sanction by re-appropriation an amount not
exceeding an amount prescribed by the Senate for an
unforeseen item not provided for in the budget and
report it to the Senate at the next meeting;
(c) to make appointments of such categories of
employees of the University and in such manner as
may be prescribed by the Statutes; to create and fill
temporary posts for a period not exceeding six
months:
Provided that appointments from (BPS-1 to
BPS-16) and administrative posts after the
commencement of this Act shall be made from
persons living within the territorial jurisdiction of the
University;
(d) to suspend, punish and remove, in accordance with
prescribed procedure, from service officers, teachers
and other employees of the University except those
appointed by or with the approval of the Senate;
(e) to delegate, subject to such conditions as may be
prescribed, any of his powers under this Act to an
officer or officers of the University; and
(f) to exercise and perform such other powers and
functions as may be prescribed.
(6) The Vice-Chancellor shall preside at the convocation of the
University in the absence of the Chancellor.
(7) The Vice-Chancellor shall present an annual report before
the Senate within three months of the close of the academic year. The
annual report shall present such information as regards the academic year
under review as may be prescribed, including disclosure of all relevant
facts pertaining to:
11
(a)academics;
(b) research;
(c) administration; and
(d) finances.
(8) The Vice-Chancellor's annual report shall be made
available, prior to its presentation before the Senate, to all officers and
University teachers and shall be published in such numbers as are required
to ensure its wide circulation.
Appointment and 13. (1) The Vice Chancellor shall be appointed by the Chancellor
Removal of the on the basis of recommendations made by the Senate.
Vice Chancellor.
(2) A search Committee for the recommendation of persons
suitable for appointment as Vice Chancellor shall be constituted by the
Senate on the date and in the manner prescribed by the Statutes and shall
consist of two eminent members of society nominated by the Chancellor,
of whom one shall further be nominated as the Convener of the
Committee, two members of the Senate, two distinguished University
Teachers who are not members of the Senate and one academic of
eminence not employed by the University. The Senate through a process
shall select the two distinguished University Teachers in such manner as
prescribed by Statute that provides for the recommendation of suitable
names by the University Teachers. The Search Committee shall remain in
existence till such time that the appointment of the next Vice Chancellor
has been made by the Chancellor.
(3) The persons proposed by the Search Committee for
appointment as Vice Chancellor shall be considered by the Senate and of
these a panel of three in order of priority, shall be recommended by the
Senate to the Chancellor:
Provided that the Chancellor may decline to appoint any of the
three persons recommended and seek recommendation of a fresh panel. In
the event of a fresh recommendation being sought by the Chancellor the
Search Committee shall make a proposal to the Senate in the Prescribed
manner.
(4) The Vice Chancellor shall be appointed for term of three
years on such terms and conditions as prescribed by Statute:
Provided that he may be reappointed for term of two years which
shall not be extended.
(5) The Senate may, pursuant to a resolution in this behalf
passed by three fourths of its membership, recommend to the Chancellor
the removal of the Vice Chancellor on the ground of inefficiency, moral
12
turpitude or physical or mental incapacity or gross misconduct, including
misuse of position for personal advantage of any kind:
Provided that the Chancellor may make a reference to the Senate
stating the instance of inefficiency, moral turpitude or physical or mental
incapacity or gross misconduct on the part of the Vice Chancellor that have
come to his notice. After consideration of the reference the Senate may,
pursuant to a resolution in this behalf passed by two-third of its
membership, recommend to the Chancellor for the removal of the Vice
Chancellor:
Provided further that prior to a resolution for the removal of the
Vice Chancellor being voted upon the Vice Chancellor shall be given a
fair opportunity of being heard.
(6) A resolution recommending the removal of the Vice
Chancellor shall be submitted to the Chancellor forthwith. The Chancellor
may accept the recommendation and order removal of the Vice Chancellor
or return the recommendation to the Senate.
(7) At any time when the office of the Vice Chancellor is
vacant, or the Vice Chancellor is absent or is unable to perform the
functions of his office due to illness or some other cause, the Pro-Vice
Chancellor shall perform the duties of the Vice Chancellor.
Pro-Vice 14. (1) The Chancellor shall appoint the Pro-Vice Chancellor of the
Chancellor. University, from amongst three senior most Professors of the University,
for a specific period not exceeding three years, which may be extended for
another term by the Chancellor.
(2) Where a Pro-Vice Chancellor is appointed under sub-section
1 he shall, notwithstanding anything contained in this Act, exercise such
powers and perform such functions of the Vice Chancellor or such other
powers and functions as the Chancellor may delegate to him.
(3) The Pro- Vice Chancellor shall be an ex-officio member of
the Syndicate and Academic Council.
Registrar. 15. (1) There shall be a Registrar of the University to be appointed
by the Senate on the recommendation of the Syndicate on such terms and
conditions as may be prescribed.
(2) The experience as well as the professional and academic
qualifications necessary for appointment to the post of the Registrar shall
be such as may be as prescribed.
(3) The Registrar shall be a full-time officer of the University and
shall:-
13
(a) be the administrative head of the secretariat of the
University and be responsible for the provision of
secretariat support to the Authorities of the
University;
(b) be the custodian of the common seal and the
academic records of the University;
(c) maintain a register of registered graduates in the
prescribed manner;
(d) supervise the process of election, appointment or
nomination of members to the various authorities and
other bodies in the prescribed manner; and
(e) perform such other duties as may be prescribed.
(4) The terms of office of the Registrar shall be for a period of
three years which may be extended for another term by Senate on the
recommendations of Syndicate
(5) The first Registrar shall be appointed by the Chancellor on
the recommendation of the Vice Chancellor.
Treasurer. 16. (1) There shall be a Treasurer of the University to be
appointed by the Senate on the recommendation of Syndicate on such
terms and conditions as may be prescribed.
(2) The experience and the professional and academic
qualifications necessary for appointment to the post of the Treasurer shall
be as may be prescribed.
(3) The Treasurer shall be the chief financial officer of the
University and shall:-
(a) manage the assets, liabilities, receipts, expenditures,
funds and investments of the University;
(b) prepare the annual and revised budget estimates of the
University and present them to the Syndicate or a
committee thereof for approval and incorporation in the
budget to be presented to the Senate;
(c) ensure that the funds of the University are expended
on the purposes for which they are provided;
(d) have the accounts of the University audited annually
so as to be available for submission to the Senate
within six months of the close of the financial year,
and
(e) perform such other duties as may be prescribed.
14
(4) The term of office of the Treasurer shall be for a period of
three years, which may be extended for another term by Senate on the
recommendations of Syndicate:
Provided that the Senate may, on the advice of the Vice-Chancellor,
terminate the appointment of the Treasurer on grounds of inefficiency or
misconduct in accordance with prescribed procedure.
Controller of 17. (1) There shall be a Controller of Examinations, to be appointed
Examinations. by the Senate on the recommendation of Syndicate on such terms and
conditions as may be prescribed.
(2) The minimum qualifications necessary for appointment to
the post of the Controller of Examinations shall be as may be prescribed.
(3) The Controller of Examinations shall be a full-time officer
of the University and shall be responsible for all matters connected with
the conduct of examinations and perform such other duties as may be
prescribed.
(4) The terms of office of the Controller of Examination shall
be for a period of three years which may be extended for another term by
Senate on the recommendations of Syndicate.
(5) The first Controller of Examination shall be appointed by
the Chancellor on the recommendation of the Vice Chancellor.
Resident Auditor. 18. The Resident Auditor shall be taken from the Office of the Auditor
General of Pakistan on deputation on such terms and conditions as
Selection Board may determine.
Director Planning 19. The Director Planning and Development shall be a whole time
and Development. officer of the University and shall be responsible for planning and
development of the University.
Appointments. 20. The University may appoint such persons in its service as may be
necessary in such manner and on such terms and conditions as may be
prescribed.
15
CHAPTER IV
AUTHORITIES OF THE UNIVERSITY.
Authorities. 21. (1) The following shall be the Authorities of the University
under this Act namely:-
(a) the Senate;
(b) the Syndicate; and
(c) the Academic Council;
(d) the Board of Studies;
(e) the Selection Board;
(f) the Finance and Planning Committee;
(g) the Advanced Studies and Research Board;
(h) the Disciplinary Committee; and
(i) Such other authorities as may be prescribed.
(2) The following shall be the Authorities that may be
established by the Statutes:-
(a) Graduate and Research Management Council;
(b) Recruitment, Development, Evaluation and
Promotion committees for teachers and other staff
whether at the level of the department, the Faculty
or the University;
(c) Career Placement and Internship Committee of
each Faculty;
(d) the Representation Committees for appointment to
the Senate, Syndicate and the Academic Council;
(e) Faculty Council; and
(f) Department Council.
(3) The Senate, the syndicate and the Academic Council may
be set up such other Committees or Sub-Committees, by whatever name
described, as considered desirable through Statutes are Regulations as
appropriate. Such Committees or Sub-Committees shall be authorities of
the University for the purposes of this Act.
Senate. 22. (1) The body responsible for the governance of the University
shall be described as the Senate, and shall consist of the following:-
(a) one sitting Judge from Balochistan High Court
nominated by Chief Justice of Balochistan;
16
(b) two assembly members from Provincial Assembly of
Balochistan nominated by the Speaker Balochistan
Assembly;
(c) the Vice Chancellor;
(d) the Pro- Vice Chancellor;
(e) the Secretary, Higher and Technical Education
Department, Government of Balochistan;
(f) the Secretary, Agriculture & Cooperatives
Department, Government of Balochistan;
(g) the Secretary, Livestock Department, Government of
Balochistan;
(h) nine elected/nominated University teaching faculty,
two Professors, two Associate Professors, two
Assistant Professors, one Academic Staff member
and two Lecturers;
(i) four persons eminent from society in the field of
Agriculture, Art, Science, engineering, medical, law
and management such that the appointment of these
persons reflects balance across the various fields;
(j) one person from amongst the alumni of Balochistan
Agriculture College/university;
(k) two persons from the academic community of the
province/ country, other than employee of the
university, and at the level of Professor or Principal
of college;
(l) one person nominated by the Commission; and
(m) the Registrar.
(2) The Chancellor shall be the chairman of the Senate.
(3) The senate shall meet at least twice in every year one dates
to be fixed by the Vice Chancellor with the consent of the Chancellor.
(4) Members of the Senate other than ex-officio members,
shall hold office for three year. One third of the members, other than ex-
officio members, of the first restructured Senate, to be determined by
secret self-assessment ballot, shall retire from office on the expiration of
one year from the date of appointment by the Chancellor. One-third of the
remaining members, other than ex-officio members, of the first
restructured Senate, to be determined by secret ballot, shall retire from the
office on the expiration of two years from the date of appointment and the
remaining one-third, other than ex officio members, shall retire from office
on the expiration of the third year:
Provided that no person, other than an ex -officio member, may
serve on the Senate for more than two consecutive terms.
17
(5) The quorum for a meeting of the Senate shall be two– third
of the total number of members: a fraction being counted as one.
(6) Service for the Senate shall be on honorary basis:
Provided that actual expenses may be reimbursed as prescribed.
Powers and Duties 23. (1) The Senate shall have the powers of general supervision over
of Senate. the University and shall hold the Vice Chancellor and the Authorities
accountable for all the functions of the University. The Senate shall have
all powers of the University not expressly vested in an Authority or officer
under this Act and all other powers not expressly mentioned in this Act
that are necessary for the performance of its functions.
(2) Without prejudice to the generality of the foregoing powers,
the Senate shall have the following powers:-
(a) to consider the drafts of Statutes and Regulations
proposed by the Syndicate and Academic Council;
(b) to consider and pass resolution on the annual report, the
annual statement of accounts, and the annual revised
budget estimates, proposed annual plan of works;
(c) to approve financial resource development plans of the
University;
(d) to appoint members to the Syndicate and other
Authorities in accordance with the provisions of this
Act;
(e) to approve the appointments/promotions of the senior
faculty and senior administration;
(f) to remove any person from the membership of any
Authority, if such person;
(i) has become unsound mind; or
(ii) has become incapacitated to function as member
of such Authority; or
(iii) has been convicted by a court of law for an
offence involving moral turpitude;
(g) to delegate any of its powers to an Authority or officer
or a committee or sub-committee; and
(h) to perform such other functions as may be prescribed by
rules.
Visitation. 24. The Senate may, in accordance with the terms and procedures as
may be prescribed, cause an inspection to be made in respect of any matter
connected with the University.
18
Syndicate. 25. (1) There shall be a Syndicate of the University consist of:-
(a) the Vice Chancellor who shall be its Chairman;
(b) the Pro-Vice Chancellor;
(c) two Members of the Provincial Assembly of
Balochistan nominated by the Speaker Balochistan
Assembly;
(d) the Deans of the Faculties of the university;
(e) one Professor from each faculty, who are not member
of the Senate, to be elected by the university teachers,
in accordance with the procedure to be prescribed by
the Senate;
(f) the Principals of constituent colleges;
(g) the Registrar;
(h) the Treasurer and;
(i) the Director Planning and Development; and
(j) the Controller of Examination.
(2) The Registrar shall be the Secretary of the Syndicate.
(3) The members of the Syndicate, other than ex-officio
members, shall hold office for three years.
(4) The Syndicate shall meet at least once in each quarter of
the year. The quorum for a meeting of the Syndicate shall be one-half of
the total number of members; a fraction being counted as one.
Powers and duties 26. (1) The Syndicate shall be the executive body of the University
of the Syndicate. and shall, subject to the provisions of this Act and statutes, take effective
measures to raise the standard of teaching, research, technological
development, publication and other academic pursuits and exercise
general supervision over the affairs of the University and management of
the property of the University.
(2) Without prejudice to the generality of the foregoing powers
and subject to the provisions of this Act, the Syndicate shall have the
powers–
(a) to hold, control and administer the property and funds
of the University;
(b) to govern and regulate, with due regard to the advice
of the Finance and Planning Committee in this behalf,
the finances, accounts and investments of the
University and for that purpose, to appoint such
agents as it may deem fit;
(c) to consider and approve the annual report, the annual
and revised budget estimates and to re-appropriate
funds from one major head of expenditure to another;
19
(d) to transfer and accept transfer of movable or
immovable property on behalf of the University;
(e) to enter into, vary, carry out or cancel contracts on
behalf of the University;
(f) to cause proper books of account to be kept for all
sums of money received and expended by the
University and for the assets and liabilities of the
University;
(g) to invest any money belonging to the University including
any unapplied income in any of the securities described in
section 20 of the Trusts Act 1882 (II of 1882) or the Trust Act
for the time being in force or of the Scheduled Commercial
Bank of the ranking as prescribed by the Finance Department,
or in the purchase of immovable property or in such other
manner, as it may determine, with the like power of varying
such investments;
(h) to receive and manage any property transferred,
grants, bequests, trusts, gifts, donations, endowments
and other contributions made to the University;
(i) to determine the form, custody and regulation of the
use of the Common Seal of the University;
(j) to provide buildings, libraries, premises, furniture,
apparatus, equipment and other means required for
carrying out the work of the University;
(k) to establish and maintain halls of residence and hostels or
approve or license hostels or lodgings for the residence of
students;
(l) to affiliate or disaffiliate Colleges and Institutes;
(m) to admit educational institutions to the privileges of
the University and withdraw such privileges;
(n) to arrange for the inspection of the academic
departments;
(o) to institute Professorships, Associate Professorships,
Assistant Professorships, Lecturer ships and other
posts or to suspend or to abolish such posts;
(p) to create, suspend or abolish such administrative,
technical, research, extension or other posts as may be
necessary;
(q) to appoint University teachers and other officers on
the recommendation of the Selection Board for
teaching and other managerial posts;
(r) to confer honorary degrees in accordance with the
Conditions prescribed;
(s) to prescribe the duties of the officers, teachers and
other employees of the University and of those
working in the University on deputation or on
contract;
20
(t) to appoint members to the various Authorities,
Committees and Bodies in accordance with the Act;
(u) to remove any person from the membership of any
authority if such person has accepted any assignment
which involves absence from the University for a
continuous period of six months or more;
(v) to regulate, determine and administer, all other
matters concerning the University and to this end
exercise all necessary powers not specifically
mentioned in this Act and statutes but not inconsistent
with the provisions of the Act;
(w) to appoint Professor Emeritus on such terms and
conditions as may be prescribed;
(x) to suspend, punish and remove from service in the
prescribed manner officers, teachers and employees
whom it is empowered to appoint;
(y) to consider and approve regulations recommended by
the Academic Council;
(z) to approve statutes and recommend those drafts of the
statutes, for submission to the Senate, which pertain to
terms and conditions of service of the University
employees;
(aa) to delegate any of its powers to any Authority or
officer or a committee or sub-committee;
(bb) to perform such other functions as may be assigned to
it under the Act or may be assigned to it by the
statutes; and
(cc) administer any funds placed at the disposal of the
university for specified purpose.
Academic Council. 27. (1) There shall be an Academic Council of the University
consisting of the following:–
(a) the Vice Chancellor who shall be its Chairperson;
(b) the Pro Vice Chancellor;
(c) the Deans of Faculties and such Head of Departments
as may be prescribed;
(d) five Professors including Professors Emeritus;
(e) five members representing the departments, institutes
and the constituent colleges to be elected in the
manner prescribed by the Senate;
(f) two Principals of affiliated colleges, one from
professional colleges;
(g) the Registrar (Member/Secretary);
(h) the Controller of Examinations;
(i) the Librarian of the University; and
21
(j) the Director, Colleges Higher & Technical
Education.
(2) The Senate shall appoint the members of the Academic
Council, other than the ex-officio and the elected members, on the
recommendation of the Vice Chancellor:
Provided that as regard the five professors and members
representing the departments, institutes and the constituent colleges the
Senate may as an alternative to elections, prescribe a procedure for
proposal of a panel of names by the Selection Committee set up in term of
section.
(3) The members of the Academic Council, other than ex-
officio members, shall hold office for three years; and if the office of any
such member becomes vacant before the expiry of the term, the vacancy
shall be filled for the remaining period in the prescribed manner.
(4) The quorum for a meeting of the Academic Council shall
be one-third of the total number of members, a fraction being counted as
one.
(5) The Academic Council shall meet in each quarter.
Powers and duties 28. (1) The Academic Council shall be the principal academic body of
of the Academic the University and shall subject to the provisions of the Act and the Statutes,
Council. have the power to lay down proper standards of instruction, research,
publication and examination and to regulate and promote the academic life of
the University and the colleges.
(2) Without prejudice to the generality of the foregoing
powers, and subject to the provisions of this Act and Statutes, the
Academic Council shall have the power to:-
(a) approve the policies and producers to the quality of
academic programs;
(b) approve academic programs;
(c) approve the policies and procedures pertaining to
student related functions including admissions,
expulsions, punishments, examinations and
certification;
(d) approve the policies and producers assuring quality
of teaching and research;
(e) recommend the policies and procedures for
affiliation of other educational institutions;
22
(f) propose to the Syndicate schemes for the constitution
and organization of faculties, teaching departments
and board of studies;
(g) appoint papers setters and examiners for all
examinations of the University after receiving panel
of names from the relevant authorities;
(h) regulate the admission of students to the courses of
studies and examinations of the University and
affiliated colleges;
(i) regulate the award of studentships, scholarships,
medals and prizes;
(j) regulate the conduct and discipline of students of the
University and affiliated colleges;
(k) propose regulations on the recommendations of the
Boards of Faculties and the Boards of Studies for
consideration and approval of the Syndicate;
(l) propose for each academic year, on the
recommendations of the Boards of Studies,
regulations prescribing the courses of studies, the
syllabi and the outlines of tests for all examinations;
provided that, if the recommendations of a Board of
Faculties or the Board of Studies are not received by
the prescribed date, the Academic Council may,
subject to the approval of the Syndicate, permit such
regulations to continue for the following years;
(m) recognize the examinations of other Universities or
examining bodies as equivalent to the corresponding
examinations of the University;
(n) appoint members to the Authorities in accordance
with the provisions of this Act;
(o) frame Regulations for submission to the Senate;
(p) prepare an annual report on the academic
performance of the University; and
(q) perform such other functions as may be prescribed
by the statutes.

function & powers no specific provision, or insufficient provision, has been made in this Act
of other shall be such as may be prescribed by the Statutes.
Authorities.

Authorities. persons who are not its members.

CHAPTER V
STATUTES, REGULATIONS AND RULES
Statutes. 31. (1) Subject to the provisions of this Act, Statutes may be made,
to regulate or prescribed all or any of the following matters:-
(a) the contents of and the manner in which the annual
report to be presented by the Vice Chancellor before the
Senate shall be prepared;
(b) the University fees and other charges;
(c) the constitution of any pension, insurance, gratuity,
provident fund and benevolent fund for University
employees;
(d) the scales of pay, method of recruitment and other terms
and conditions of service of officers, teachers and other
employees of the University;
(e) the maintenance of register of students and registered
graduates;
(f) affiliation and disaffiliation of colleges, institutes, etc.
and related matters;
(g) conduct of elections for membership of Authorities of
the University and related matters;
(h) admission of educational institutions to the privileges
of the University and the withdrawal of such
privileges;
(i) the establishment of faculties, colleges, institutes,
departments and academic divisions;
(j) the powers and duties of officers, teachers and
employees of the University;
(k) conditions under which the University may enter into
arrangements with public bodies or other
organizations for the purposes of research and
advisory services;
(l) conditions for appointment of Emeritus Professors
and Meritorious Professors and award of honorary
degrees;
(m) conduct and discipline of the officers, teachers and
other employees of the University;
(n) the constitution, powers and duties of the Authorities
and conduct of elections to such Authorities and
related matters;
(o) constitution, functions and powers of the Authorities
of the University;
(p) general scheme of studies including the duration of
courses, the system of examinations and the number
of subjects and papers for examinations; and
24
(q) all other matters which are to be or may be prescribed
or regulated by statutes.
(2) The draft of the Statutes shall be proposed by the Syndicate
to the Senate which may approve or pass with such modification as the
Senate may think fit or may refer it back to the Syndicate as the case may
be, for reconsideration of the proposed draft:
Provided that Statutes concerning any of the matter mentioned in
clauses (a) and (m) of sub section (1) shall be initiated and approved by
the Senate, after seeking the views of the Syndicate:
Provided further that the Senate may initiate statutes with respect
to any matter in the power or with respect to which a Statute may be framed
in terms of the Act approve such Statute after seeking the views of the
Syndicate.
Regulations. 32. (1) Subject to the provisions of this Act and the statutes, the
Academic Council may make Regulations, which shall be published in the
official Gazette for all or any of the following matters:-
(a) the courses of study for degrees, diplomas and certificates
of the University;
(b) the manner and method of teaching conducted in the
University and affiliated colleges;
(c) the admission of students to the University and
conditions under which they are admitted or allowed
to take courses and examinations of the University
and become eligible for the award of degrees,
diplomas and certificates;
(d) fees and other charges to be paid by students for
admission to the courses of studies and the
examinations of the University;
(e) the conduct of examinations;
(f) the conduct and discipline of students of the
University;
(g) conditions of residence of the students of the University
or colleges including the levying of fee for residence in
halls of residence and hostels and approval of hostels, and
lodgings for students;
(h) conditions for acquiring research degrees;
(i) institution of fellowships, scholarships, medals and
prizes;
(j) institution of stipends and free and half-free
studentships;
(k) academic costume;
25
(l) use of the library;
(m) the formation of teaching departments and Boards of
Studies; and
(n) all other matters which under the Act or the statutes
are to be or may be prescribed by regulations.
(2) The Academic Council shall prepare and submit the
regulations to the Syndicate and Senate, which may approve them with
or without modifications or refer them back to the Academic Council for
reconsideration or reject them. No Regulation shall be valid unless it has
been approved by the Syndicate.
(3) Regulations regarding or incidental to matters contained in
sub-clauses (i) and (m) of sub section (1) shall not be submitted to the
Senate without the prior approval of the Syndicate.
Amendment and 33. The procedure for adding to, amending or repealing the Statutes and
Repeal of Statutes Regulations shall be the same as prescribed respectively for framing or
and Regulations. making Statutes and Regulations.
Rules. 34. (1) The Authorities and the other bodies of the University may
make Rules, to be published in the official Gazette, consistent with the Act,
Statutes or the Regulations, to regulate any matter relating to the affairs of
the University which has not been provided for by the Act or that is not
required to be regulated by Statutes or Regulations, including rules to
regulate the conduct of business and the time and place of meetings and
related matters.
(2) Rules shall become effective upon approval by the
Syndicate.
CHAPTER VI
AFFILIATION OF EDUCATIONAL
INSTITUTION TO THE UNIVERSITY
Affiliations. 35. (1) An educational institution seeking affiliation to the
University shall make an application satisfying the University that–
(a) the educational institution is under the management
of Government or a regularly constituted governing
body;
(b) the financial resources of the educational institution are
sufficient to ensure its continued maintenance and
efficient working;
(c) the strength and qualifications and the terms and
conditions of service of the teaching and other staff of
the educational institution are satisfactory for the
26
purpose of teaching of prescribed courses of studies
and training in the institution;
(d) the educational institution has framed proper rules
governing the conduct and discipline of its
employees;
(e) the building of the educational institution is suitable
and commodious for its requirements;
(f) the educational institution has, or can make, a
provision in the prescribed manner for the residence
of students not residing with their parents or
guardians, and their supervision and physical and
general welfare;
(g) the educational institution has a provision for a
library and adequate library service;
(h) the educational institution has properly equipped
laboratories, museums and other places of practical
work required for courses of studies taught in the
educational institution;
(i) the educational institution has, or can make, provision
for the residence of its Principal/Director and other
members of the teaching staff in the educational
institution building or near such building or the
residence of students; and
(j) the affiliation of the educational institution shall not
be injurious to the education or discipline of the
students of other institutions in the neighborhood.
(2) The application shall further contain an undertaking by the
educational institution that after the institution is affiliated, any change in
the management or the teaching staff shall forthwith be reported to the
University and that the teaching staff shall possess such qualifications as
are, or may be, prescribed.
(3) The Senate shall after considering the recommendations of
the Affiliation Committee, dispose of the application for affiliation in
accordance with such procedure as may be prescribed and may grant or refuse
affiliation:
Provided that the affiliation shall not be refused, unless the
educational institution has been given an opportunity of making a
representation against the proposed decision.
Extension of 36. Where an affiliated college desires to add to the courses of studies
affiliation. in respect of which it is granted affiliation, the procedure prescribed for
affiliation of colleges shall as far as possible may be followed.
27
Inspection and 37. (1) Every affiliated educational institution shall furnish such
reports. reports, returns and other information as the University may require to enable
it to judge the efficiency of the educational institution.
(2) The University may call upon any affiliated educational
institution to take, within a specified period, such action in respect of any
matter mentioned in sub-section (2) of section 35as the University may
deem fit.
Disaffiliation. 38. (1) Where any affiliated educational institution has failed to
fulfill any requirement of this Act, or has failed to observe any of the
conditions of affiliation or its affairs are conducted in a manner prejudicial
to the interests of education, the Syndicate may, in the prescribed manner,
and after considering any representation that the educational institution
may wish to make, modify or withdraw all or any of the privileges
conferred on the educational institution by the affiliation.
(2) The procedure to be followed for the withdrawal of affiliation
shall be such as may be prescribed.
Appeal against 39. Where any educational institution has been refused affiliation or all or
refusal or any of the privileges conferred on any educational institution by affiliation
withdrawal of have been modified or withdrawn it may, within the prescribed period, apply
affiliation. for review to the Syndicate against such refusal and the application shall be
disposed of in such manner as may be prescribed.
CHAPTER -VII
FINANCIAL PROVISIONS.
University Fund. 40. (1) The University has a fund to which shall be credited its income
from fees, donations, trusts, bequest, endowments, contributions, grants
and all other sources.
(2) The budgetary allocations of the operating expenses of erstwhile
College, before the commencement of this Act shall be provided to the university
as grant with appropriate annual increase as deemed appropriate by Government.
These funds shall be transferred to the account of the university on bi-annual
basis.
Provided that the employees related expenses of erstwhile
college shall be budgeted separately under the university.
(3) The University may accept donations in the shape of land,
vehicle, equipment or any other item that may facilitate the functioning of
28
the University and all such donations shall be used, maintained and
disposed of by the University in the prescribed manner.
(4) All pre-operating costs incurred in connection with the
affairs of the University shall be deemed to have been incurred for all
intends and purposes from the University Funds and shall be a valid charge
on the University Fund.
Recovery of 41. The University or any person generally or specially authorized by it
University may apply to the Collector for recovery of any sum due to the University
Dues. and the Collector shall thereupon proceed to recover the sum due, as if it
were an arrear of land revenue:
Provided that the University shall not take any action unless the
person concerned is given an opportunity of being heard.
Budget, audit and 42. (1) The budget of the University shall be approved and its
accounts. accounts shall be maintained and audited in such manner as may be
prescribed.
(2) The teaching departments, constituent colleges/institutes
and all other bodies designated as such by the Syndicate in terms of
Statutes shall be independent cost centers of the University with authority
vested in the head of each cost center to sanction expenditure out of the
budget allocated to it
Provided that re-appropriation from one head of
expenditure to another may be made by the head of a cost center in
accordance with and to the extent prescribed by the Statutes.
(3) All funds generated by a teaching department, constituent
college or other unit of the University through consultancy, research or
other provision of service shall be made available without prejudice to the
budgetary allocation otherwise made, after deduction of overheads in the
manner and to the extent prescribed by Statute, to the teaching department,
constituent college or other unit for its development. A part of the funds
so generated may be shared with the University teachers or researchers in
charge of the consultancy, research or service concerned in the manner and
to the extent prescribed by Statute.
(4) No expenditure shall be made from the funds of the
University, unless the Resident Auditor in confirmatory with the statutes,
regulations and rules has in the prescribed manner, audited a bill for
payment. The Treasure has verified that the payment is provided for in the
approved budget of the cost center, subject to the authority to re-
appropriate available to the head of the cost center.
29
(5) Provision shall be made for an internal audit of the finances
of the University.
(6) Without prejudice to the requirement of audit by an auditor
appointed by Government in accordance with the provisions of any
other law in force, the annual audited statement of accounts of the
University shall be prepared in conformity with the Generally
Accepted Accounting Principles (GAAP) by a reputed firm of
chartered accountants and signed by the Treasurer. The annual
audited statement of accounts so prepared shall be submitted to the
Auditor General of Pakistan for his observations.
(7) The observations of the Auditor General of Pakistan, if any,
together with such annotations as the Treasurer may make, shall be
considered by the Syndicate and shall be placed before the Senate within
six months of closing of the financial year. Syndicate may approve the
budget of the University, appropriations of accounts of the University and
settle an audit para relating to the audit of the University.
(8) The Syndicate may delegate the power of appropriation or
re-appropriation of funds to an officer of the University.
CHAPTER- VIII
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Opportunity 43. Except as otherwise provided by law no officer, teacher or other
to show cause. employee of the University holding a permanent post shall be reduced in rank,
dismissed or removed from service or compulsorily retired from service for
cause arising out of any act or omission on the part of the person concerned
unless he/she has been given a reasonable opportunity of showing cause
against the action proposed to be taken.
Appeal to and 44. (1) Where an order is passed punishing any officer (other than
review by the the Vice Chancellor), or any teacher or employee of the University or
Syndicate and altering or interpreting to his disadvantage the prescribed terms or conditions
Senate. of his service, he shall, where the order is passed by any other officer or
teacher of the University (other than the Vice Chancellor), have the right to
appeal to the Syndicate against the order, and where the order is made/passed
by the Vice Chancellor, have the right to apply to Senate.
(2) The application for review shall be submitted to the Vice
Chancellor who shall refer it to the Syndicate/Senate with such
recommendation as the Vice Chancellor may consider necessary.
30
(3) No order on an appeal or application for review shall be
passed without affording to the appellant or petitioner, as the case may be,
an opportunity of being heard and an appeal against the order is not
provided under the statutes or regulations, any aggrieved person may
prefer an appeal against the order to the Syndicate.
Service of the 45. (1) All persons employed by the University in accordance with
University and the terms and conditions of service prescribed by statutes shall be persons
retirement from in the service of Pakistan for the purposes of any court or tribunal set up
service. by law in terms of Article 212 of the Constitution of the Islamic Republic
of Pakistan, 1973:
Provided that any provision as regards the terms and conditions of
employment of persons in the service of Pakistan in general or in
comparable employment notwithstanding the service of persons employed
by the University shall be entirely governed by the terms and conditions
prescribed by the relevant Statutes.
(2) An officer, other than the Vice Chancellor, teacher or other
employee of the University shall retire from service-
(a) on such date, after he/she has completed twenty five
years of service qualifying for pension or other
retirement benefits as the competent authority may, in
the public interest, direct:
Provided that no employee shall be retired unless
he has been informed in writing of the grounds of the
disciplinary action proposed to be taken against him/her
and has been given reasonable opportunity of showing
cause against that action ; or
(b) where no direction is given under clause (a), on the
completion of the sixtieth year of his age.
Explanation.– In this section, “competent authority” means the
appointing authority or a person duly authorized by the appointing
authority in that behalf, not being a person lower in rank to the officer,
teacher or other employee concerned.
(3) No adverse change shall be made in the terms and
conditions of employment of any University Teacher in the employment
of the University on the date of enforcement of the Act.
31
Pension, 46. (1) The University shall constitute for the benefit of its
Insurance, officers, teachers and other employees schemes, as may be prescribed, for
gratuity, the provision of post- employment benefits such as pension, group
provident fund insurance, gratuity, provident fund, benevolent fund and any other scheme
and as it may deem fit.
Benevolent fund.
(2) Where any provident fund has been constituted under this
Act, the provisions of the Provident Fund Act, 1925 (XIX of 1925), shall
apply to such fund as if it were a Government Provident Fund and the
University were the Government.
Commencement 47. (1) When a member of an Authority is elected, appointed or
of term of office nominated, his/her term of office, as fixed under this Act, shall commence
of members of on such date as may be prescribed.
authorities.
(2) Where a member who has accepted any other assignment
or for any other similar reason remains absent from the University for a
period of not less than six months he shall be deemed to have resigned and
vacated his seat.
Filling of casual 48. Any casual vacancy among the elected, appointed or nominated members
vacancies in of any authority shall be filled as soon as conveniently may be, in the same
authorities. manner and by the same person or the authority that had elected, appointed or
nominated the member whose place has become vacant and the person elected,
appointed or nominated to the vacancy shall be a member of such authority for
the residue of the term for which the person whose place he fills would have been
a member.
Filling of vacancies 49. Where a vacancy in the membership of an Authority cannot be filled
in authorities in because of–
certain
circumstances. (a) the office, the holder whereof was to be a member of the Authority
ex-officio, having ceased to exist; or
(b) the organization, institution or other body, other than the
University having either ceased to exist or to function; or
(c) the occurrence of other circumstances in which it has become
impracticable to fill the vacancy, the vacancy shall be filled in
such manner as the Chancellor may direct.
Flaws in the 50. Where there is a flaw in the constitution of an Authority, as constituted by
constitution of this Act, the Statutes or the Regulations on account of the abolition of a specified
authorities. office under Government or because an organization, institution or other body
outside the University has been dissolved or has ceased to function, or because of
some other similar reason, such flaw shall be removed in such manner as the
Senate may direct.
32
Tripartite 51. (1) Any officer, teacher of the Government or employee of the
mobility. University, on the recommendation of the Syndicate, may be directed by the
concerned Government Department with approval of competent authority or
university as the case may be, to serve in any post in the University, under the
Government or an educational research institution in the public interest:
Provided that the terms and conditions offered to him/her shall not
be less favorable than those enjoyed by him/her immediately before his
services are placed at the disposal of the University and full benefit of
his/her previous service shall continue to remain in force until amended or
repealed.
(2) The concerned Government Department with the approval
of competent authority may, in consultation with the Selection Board,
place the services of an employee of the Government or any other
University or an educational or research institution, at the disposal of the
University in the public interest:
Provided that the terms and conditions offered to him shall not be
less favorable than those enjoyed by him immediately before his/her
services are placed at the disposal of the University and that full benefit of
his/her previous service shall be allowed to him/her.
Proceedings of 52. No act, proceeding, resolution or decision of any Authority shall be
authorities not invalid by reason only of any vacancy on the authority doing ,passing, or
invalidated by making it or by reason of any want of qualification or invalidity in the
vacancies. election, appointment or nomination of any de facto member of the
Authority where present or absent.
Indemnity. 53. No suit or legal proceeding shall lie against the Government, the
University or any Authority, officer or employee of Government or the
University or any person in respect of anything, which is done in good faith
under this Act.
Savings. 54. (1) Notwithstanding anything contained in any other law, for
the time being in force upon coming into force of this Act, anything done,
action taken, all funds, properties, rights and interests of whatsoever kind
issued, used, enjoyed, possessed, owned or vested in the Balochistan
Agriculture College, Quetta existing immediately before the
commencement of this Act and all liabilities subsisting against the said
College shall stand transferred to the University established under this Act.
(2) Everything done, action taken, obligations and
liabilities incurred, rights and assets acquired, persons appointed or
authorized, jurisdictions or powers conferred, endowments, bequests,
funds or trusts created, donations or grants made, Scholarships,
Studentships or exhibitions instituted, affiliations or privileges granted and
orders issued under any of the provisions of the Statutes, Regulations and
33
Rules made or deemed to have been made there under or any other law
made applicable to the Balochistan Agriculture College, Quetta, shall, if
not inconsistent with the provisions of this Act or Statutes, Regulations or
Rules made under this Act, be continued and, so far as may be, be deemed
to have been respectively done, taken incurred, acquired, appointed or
authorized, conferred, created, made, instituted granted and issued under
this Act, and any documents referring to any of the provisions existing
Rules and Regulations first referred shall, so far as may be, be considered
to refer corresponding provisions of this Act or Statues, Regulations and
Rules made under this Act.
First Statutes and 55. Notwithstanding anything to the contrary contained in this Act, the
Regulations. First Statutes, set out in the Schedule appended to this Act shall be deemed to
be the Statutes framed under section 31 of this Act and shall continue to
remain in force until altered, amended or repealed by new statues in
accordance to the provisions of the Act:
Provided that till such time the Authorities mentioned in sections
31, 32 and 34 are not constituted, the Chancellor shall be the authority for
making Statues, Regulations and Rules in accordance with the provisions of
the Act.
Transitory 56. (1) Notwithstanding anything contained in the Act, upon
Provisions. the coming into force of this Act with respect to University of Agriculture
Quetta, the Senate shall be established and the members thereof, except the
University Teachers, appointed by the Chancellor in accordance with the
numbers and criteria for membership specified in the Act. The University
Teachers shall be appointed to the first Senate by the Chancellor. The
number of University Teachers to be appointed to the first Senate shall be
appointed as soon as the procedure prescribed for appointment of
University Teachers to the Senate can be complied with. The first Senate
so constituted shall initiate, as soon as possible, the process for the
appointment of the members of the Syndicate and the Academic Council
in accordance with the terms of this Act. The term of tenure provided in
sub-section (4) of section 22 notwithstanding, one-third of the members,
other than ex-officio members, of the first Senate, to be determined by lot,
shall retire from office on the expiration of one year from the date of
appointment by the Chancellor. One-half of the remaining members, other
than ex-officio members, of the first Senate, to be determined by lot, shall
retire from office on the expiration of two years from the date of
appointment and the remaining one-half, other than ex-officio members,
shall retire from office on the expiration of the third year.
(2) Notwithstanding anything contained in this Act the first
Vice Chancellor shall be appointed by the Chancellor for a period of one
year as prescribed in the Act.
34
(3) Notwithstanding anything contained in this Act, the first
appointments to the statutory posts of Pro Vice Chancellor, Registrar,
Treasurer and Controller of Examination may be made by the Chancellor
for the period of one year specified under the Act in his discretion:
Provided that the persons to be appointed on the above mentioned statutory
posts must fulfill all the laid down criteria required for the posts.
Removal of 57. (1) If any question arises as to the interpretation of any of the
difficulties. provisions of the Act, it shall be placed before the Chancellor whose
decision thereon shall be final.
(2) If any difficulty arises in giving effect to any of the
provisions of the Act, the Chancellor may make such order after obtaining
the views of the Senate, not inconsistent with the provisions of the Act, as
may appear to him to be necessary for removing the difficulty.
(3) Where the Act makes any provision for anything to be done
but no provision or no sufficient provision has been made as respects the
authority by whom, or the time at which, or the manner in which it shall
be done, then it shall be done by such authority, at such time, or in such
manner as the Chancellor may direct after obtaining the views of the
Senate.
Power to allow 58. (1) Notwithstanding anything contained in this Act the Senate
appointment of may, on the advice of the Syndicate, allow any post in the University to be
employees of filled by appointment, on such terms as the Senate may specify, an
Government, employee of the Government or any other university or educational or
other universities research institution:
or educational or
research Provided that in the case of a teacher the selection board shall be
institutions to the consulted before filling of the post; and
university and vice
versa. (2) Any officer, teacher or other employee of the University
shall, as the Chancellor may in the public interest direct, serve in any post
under Government or any other University or an Educational or Research
Institution:
Provided that Syndicate shall be consulted before issuing the
direction.
(3) Where any appointment has been made under this section,
the terms and conditions of service of the appointee shall not be less
favorable than those admissible to him/her immediately before such
appointment and he shall be entitled to all benefits of his/her post of
service.
